userStories.title: Delete the deferred regression gate
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Remove the deferred regression gate, its completion options/status inputs, and its exclusively owned implementation and tests.

**Motivation** — After B1 the post-run phases still sit in the tree and still compile, but no production path runs them.

**Approach** — Removal only. Each phase is deleted importer-first: the first story of a phase cuts the live references and deletes the modules nothing else imports; the next stories delete the modules the earlier ones imported. Every story leaves a tree that compiles and passes the suite. No story adds a feature or changes a workflow-mode result.

### Part 1: the deferred regression gate (US-001)

| Site | After |
|:---|:---|
| `handleRunCompletion` phase 1 (`execution/lifecycle/run-completion.ts:198-213`) | removed; `regressionGateFailed` is gone, and `hooksConfig` leaves the destructure at `:195` |
| `_runCompletionDeps.runDeferredRegression` (`run-completion.ts:55`) and the imports at `:47-48` | removed |
| `RunCompletionOptions.skipRegression` (`run-completion.ts:78-79`) | removed |
| the `writeFinalStatus` call (`run-completion.ts:293-301`) | no `regressionGateFailed` argument |
| `writeFinalStatus` (`execution/lifecycle/run-completion-phases.ts:481-497`) | the `regressionGateFailed` input goes; the status ladder starts at `exitReason === "cost-limit"` |
| the `handleRunCompletion` call in `runCompletionPhase` (`runner-completion.ts:376`) | no `skipRegression` |
| barrels `execution/lifecycle/index.ts`, `execution/index.ts` | drop the re-exports of deleted symbols |

Delete:

- `packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-completion-regression.ts`
- `packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression-phases.ts`
- `packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-regression-triage.ts`

**Scope** — In: the Part 1 cuts, declarations, barrels, corresponding tests and stale checker references. Out: finish-machine removal (US-002–US-004), acceptance blocks/loop/core (US-005–US-007), per-story regression/full-suite verification, phase-name registries and regression configuration keys.

**Interface** — `RunCompletionOptions` (`run-completion.ts`). Target: the baseline fields minus `skipRegression`. `writeFinalStatus` target: `(input: { options: RunCompletionOptions; prd: PRD; statusWriter: StatusWriter; config: NaxConfig; reportedTotal: number; iterations: number }): Promise<void>`. Keep `handleRunCompletion(options: RunCompletionOptions): Promise<RunCompletionResult>` as the existing entry point.

Retain hook-order, payload, cost-limit and manifest-retention assertions. In lifecycle/run-completion-backfill.test.ts remove the regression-cost-merge describe and the overall-regression-success fallback case; retain metric backfill. In lifecycle/run-completion-edges.test.ts remove regression-gate throw, on-final-regression-fail and skipRegression describes and the two regression storyMetrics projection cases; retain other edges. In lifecycle/run-completion-events.test.ts remove regression completed-event mode/failedTests describes; retain review events and durations. Remove runDeferredRegression stubs and DeferredRegressionResult imports from all of those files and lifecycle/run-completion-fallback.test.ts, run-completion-mcp-adoption.test.ts, run-completion-plugin-review.test.ts, run-completion-session-close.test.ts and acceptance-loop-skipped-packages.test.ts, preserving their other assertions until the acceptance-loop file is deleted in US-006. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Finish the acceptance deletion by removing unused core modules and result fields, dropping the features resolve acceptance block, and retaining nax accept only as a fail-fast removal message.

**Motivation** — `nax accept` overrides failed acceptance criteria that a workflow run never produces.

**Approach** — US-007 deletes the acceptance modules nothing still imports, `nax accept` and the resolve block, and removes `acceptancePassed`:

| Site | After |
|:---|:---|
| `ResolveResult.acceptance` (`cli/features-resolve.ts:43-44`), the `acceptance:` properties (`:267`, `:323`), the import (`:6`) | removed |
| `RunnerCompletionResult.acceptancePassed` (`runner-completion.ts:103-106`) and its return | removed |
| the run result in `run` (`execution/runner.ts:384`, `:395`) | `success: isComplete(prd) && !pluginGateFailed && workflowPassed !== false` |
| `src/cli/index.ts` | the `accept` re-export (`:5`) and the `features-acceptance` re-exports (`:106-112`) go |
| `src/test-runners/index.ts:13-15`, `:17-18` | the `ac-coverage`, `ac-parser` and `compile-crash` re-exports go; `createTestFileClassifier` (`:16`) stays |
| `src/acceptance/index.ts`, `prompts/index.ts`, `config/index.ts` | drop the re-exports of the deleted symbols |
| `scripts/check-inline-test-mocks.ts` | entries naming a deleted test file go |
| `../repo-tooling/scripts/check-package-frame-derivation.ts:71-74` | the `src/cli/features-acceptance.ts` allowance goes |

`nax accept` stays declared in `bin/nax.ts` (`:1337-1355`) so a user gets the removal message instead of commander's unknown-command error. Its three options become plain `.option(...)` calls (not `requiredOption`), its description becomes `Removed: workflow mode does not run acceptance tests`, and its action prints, in red on stderr, `nax accept was removed: workflow mode does not run acceptance tests`, then exits 1. It reads no config and no PRD. The `acceptCommand` import (`bin/nax.ts:45`) goes.

Refine-pass audit: re-read the on-disk spec's Integration, Failure Handling, Out of Scope, Context Files and all eight stated ACs, and cross-checked the retained runtime/tests. Spec AC inventory and mapping (numbers refer to each story's acceptanceCriteria): US-005.1 maps to US-005 AC1 (completed exit) and AC2 (no pre-run log), preserving non-dry-run, resolved workflow preflight, hand-built acceptance.enabled:true and the pending-story runIteration stub. US-005.2 maps to AC3 (max-iterations exit) and AC4 (no post-run log), retaining the critical unchanged PRD and prdDirty:false on every iteration. US-006.1 maps to US-006 AC1, retaining the complete PRD, non-dry-run, recording status writer, enabled config and explicit prohibition on assigning an acceptance dependency. US-007.1 maps to US-007 AC1-2 (exact option-bearing spawn, empty cwd, exit 1, stderr). US-007.2 maps to AC3-5 (bare spawn, empty cwd, exit 1, stderr, no required-option error). US-007.3 maps to AC7 and AC10-12 (named resolution status, patterns, message prefix and own-key absence); AC8-9 additionally preserve the Failure Handling table's featureName and specSource fields. US-007.4 maps to AC13-15 (exactly-one-feature auto-discovery status, featureName and own-key absence). US-007.5 maps to AC16 (complete-PRD completion result has no own acceptancePassed key). No original criterion or qualifying clause was dropped; no deprecated file-content tags occur. The remaining Failure Handling rows are covered by the no-read binary probe, absent acceptance stage:enter events in US-005 and absent acceptance phase events/status in US-006.

The requested refine audit requires a negative-path AC in every story, overriding the original spec's criteria-free treatment of US-001 through US-004 only to pin existing behavior: cost-limit status with pending work (US-001), thrown feature-workflow failure outcome (US-002), empty quality commands returning passed:false (US-003), and git commit failure rejection (US-004). These are regression checks in retained tests, not new functionality or new source/test files. Evidence: packages/nax/test/unit/execution/lifecycle-completion.test.ts:573-586; execution/end-phase.test.ts:257-264; packages/nax/src/finish/gates/quality.ts:313-320; packages/nax/test/unit/finish/commit.test.ts:102-114 and src/finish/commit.ts:150-156. US-005 retains the max-iterations negative case. US-006 adds an unusable legacy status-reader case observed via zero getPostRunStatus calls. US-007 has both removed-command failures, including the missing-options form. Vague no-stage/no-loop statements were made observable through existing event emitters; the no-read CLI statement now uses a test-only filesystem-read recorder rather than assuming empty cwd proves no access. No production instrumentation is authorized.

All nine feature-level exclusions match the spec verbatim in outOfScope, with no story-local deferral hoisted into them. All seven exact binding IDs, workdirs and dependencies are unchanged; the serial chain is required by importer-depth deletion, not an optional planning preference. Complexity remains complex because each story deletes multiple modules and edits shared importers/fixtures, rather than because of AC count. Lite isolated testing is the lightest realistic default for that fan-out; US-003 and US-004 retain strict isolation because they remove acceptance-edit guards/filesystem-containment helpers adjacent to retained safety behavior.
